messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] gpu-queue-exhaustion prod-serving-cluster — queue_length=124, pending_pods=78, autoscaler_status=ScaleUpFailed, reason=attachRolePropagationTimeout. Paging oncall.
maya: @sam i see the page — looking now. queue growth started ~10:12 UTC, spikes correlate with a large rerank batch from customer-xyz.
sam: pulling cluster-autoscaler logs, give me a sec. running kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler | tail -n 100
sam: ```
I0410 10:14:28 main.go:xxxx] ScaleUp: pod(s) didn't fit, node group gpu-prod-asg: insufficient resources: gpu
E0410 10:14:30 scale_up.go:xxx] Failed to launch instance: LaunchTemplateVersionMismatch: version 5 not found in Launch Template lt-prod-gpu
E0410 10:14:30 scale_up.go:xxx] AttachRolePropagationTimeout: waiting for instance profile to be available
W0410 10:14:31 main.go:xxxx] Retryable failure, backing off
```
sam: looks like two simultaneous problems: launch template version mismatch and IAM/PassRole propagation delays.
ale x: (joining) can you paste the ASG / LT config? might be from yesterday's rollout.
maya: I rolled a launch template update at 02:00 UTC for gpu-prod-asg (version 5) but we reverted to v3 earlier today after perf regressions — maybe the autoscaler still references v5.
lee: checking autoscaler configmap: kubectl -n kube-system get configmap cluster-autoscaler-status -o yaml | grep -A2 launch
lee: autoscaler is referencing nodeGroup config with LaunchTemplateVersion: "$Latest" in cloudprovider config — that should pick latest, but ASG attached LT pinned to v3. mismatch possible on rapid rollbacks.
sam: also see repeated IAM errors from the node creation path: "ec2:RunInstances: AccessDenied - iam:PassRole" in CloudTrail at 10:13:52. suggests instance profile/role propagation problem.
alex: can we confirm instance profile exists and is attached to the LT? aws iam get-instance-profile --instance-profile-name gpu-node-role-prod -> ok. But cloud-init logs show permission denied during attach.
maya: immediate mitigation options: 1) increase ASG desired capacity to spawn existing compatible instances (bypass LT version mismatch), 2) manually launch a temporary on-demand GPU instance with correct profile, 3) scale down low-priority/evictable pods to free GPUs.
sam: I'll try (1) first: aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-prod-asg --desired-capacity 6 --honor-cooldown
sam: result: "SetDesiredCapacity: capacity 4 -> 6 requested". ASG started launching, but some launches failed with LaunchTemplate error. 2/2 launched succeeded with v3.
sam: meanwhile i'm manually creating an on-demand instance as hotfix: aws ec2 run-instances --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abcd1234 --version 3 --instance-type p3.2xlarge --iam-instance-profile Name=gpu-node-role-prod
sam: run-instances returned instance i-0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7g (pending). tagging it kube-node with label node.kubernetes.io/gpu=present.
lee: kubelet on that instance registered, pods started scheduling, queue drained a bit. queue_length -> 64 in 6m. nice.
maya: still seeing ~10 pods stuck Pending with tolerations for nvidia-gpu taint: node.kubernetes.io/gpu:NoSchedule — describe shows they tolerate but affinity to GPU resource missing on some pods.
sam: forced eviction of low-priority batch pods: kubectl -n prod delete pod -l job=batch-rerank --grace-period=0 --force; freed ~8 GPUs.
customer-bridge: customer-xyz support channel: customers A/B seeing 500s and higher latency. alerted customer success, posting status update: "We're seeing degraded throughput for reranking jobs; mitigation in progress — ETA 20m" :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maya: turning on temporary fallback: route rerank jobs to smaller model (cpu-only) for non-critical jobs. Patch applied to traffic-router, reducing load on GPU queue.
sam: cluster-autoscaler leader election logs show frequent leader changes — looks like the CA pod restarts on node pressure causing scale attempts to abort. Restart reason: OOMKilled (peak memory ~1.8Gi).
lee: bumped CA memory request/limit from 200Mi->800Mi and restarted deployment. also increased leader lease duration to 60s to reduce thrash.
sam: re-checking IAM propagation: create-instance-profile-role ran at 02:00 but has eventual consistency delays. I'll add an exponential backoff in our LT rollout pipeline and add a step to wait for iam:PassRole to succeed via a test run.
alex: for immediate stability we should pin autoscaler to LT version 3 explicitly to avoid $Latest confusion until rollout pipeline is hardened.
maya: agreed. created PR to pin LaunchTemplateVersion=3 in cloudprovider config, will apply on next small window. (PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/384)
customer-bridge: update posted: "Mitigations applied: new nodes added, low-priority jobs evicted, temporary model fallback enabled. Impact reduced. Next update in 30m."
pagerduty-bot: @maya acknowledged the pager. Escalation to SRE oncall in 30m if status not green.
sam: monitoring shows queue_length down to 18, pending pods 6, pod start latency improved. error rate for customer-xyz dropped from 6% -> 1.2%.
lee: handoff: i'm taking over oncall for next 45m to watch for reoccurrence. summary: root cause = rollout/rollbacks + LT version resolution + IAM passrole propagation + CA instability under memory pressure. Immediate fixes applied: manual node launches, ASG desired bump, eviction of low-priority jobs, CA mem bump, temporary model fallback, pin LT version. Next actions: hardened rollout pipeline, add IAM propagation test, autoscaler unit tests for LT mismatch, increase CA replica resilience.
maya: thanks @lee. i've notified support and engineering leads. will open a postmortem and tag infra/eng-runtime/eng-sre. please add any notes here.
alex: adding one note — consider an autoscaler preflight that validates LT/ASG alignment before scaling decisions; i can sketch an RFC tomorrow.
lee: will check in 20m; if stable, we'll close pager. :white_check_mark:
maya: final: thanks everyone. incident closed for paging at 10:47 UTC, we'll follow up with full postmortem. :thumbsup:
